findings.title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET with no token
findings.body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe immediately writes the current user's TopicUser notification level, and check_xhr is skipped so a normal browser navigation (and cross-site requests that send the session cookie) can hit it. Mail-security scanners and link prefetchers issue GETs on email links, and any site can embed the URL to mute or demote a logged-in victim's topic notifications without CSRF protection. The link in the email is exactly this URL, so opening or previewing the message can change notification state before the user chooses anything. Unsubscribe needs a non-prefetchable method (POST) and a user-bound token, or a confirmation page that does not mutate on GET.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser exists
findings.body: unsubscribe loads TopicUser with find_by and then calls tu.notification_level and tu.save! with no nil check. Users who were emailed but have no topic_users row (or whose row was removed) get a NoMethodError instead of an unsubscribe. The action should create the row (TopicUser.change / find_or_initialize) and set the level, including the notifications_changed_at / reason fields that change() normally writes.

findings.title: Watching and tracking users are not actually unsubscribed
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), the action sets it to regular instead of muted. Those are the users who receive per-topic notification mail, and the new email copy says the link will stop notifications for this topic. One click only demotes them to regular, so reply, mention, and quote mail can continue. A second click is required to mute, and nothing in the email says that. The link should set muted (or whatever level truly stops topic mail) in one request.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template is not resolved for the new route
findings.body: The Ember route is registered as topicUnsubscribe (path /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe), whose controller, route, and view are topic-unsubscribe. This template lives at topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which the resolver binds to a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was never defined. After the server renders the app shell, the client route has no template, so the confirmation copy and the topic-notifications-button never render. Move the template to topic-unsubscribe.hbs (or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and point the URL there).

findings.title: No tests for the unsubscribe action
findings.body: The new endpoint changes notification level, redirects on slug mismatch, and is linked from every notification email, but the only spec change is passing unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder. There is no coverage for missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted, unauthenticated access, or the slug redirect. Those paths can 500 or leave the user subscribed without a failing test.
